video.title: Cell Reproduction: From One Cell to Two

scenes.title: Cell Reproduction: Overview
scenes.narration: Cell reproduction allows organisms to grow, replace damaged cells, and continue life. In eukaryotic cells, this process is coordinated through the cell cycle, where genetic material is copied and carefully distributed.

elements.title: Controlled Duplication
elements.detail: Genetic information is copied before the cell separates.

scenes.title: The Cell Cycle: Interphase to Mitosis
scenes.narration: The cell cycle contains interphase and the mitotic phase. During interphase, the cell grows, duplicates its DNA, and prepares for division. The mitotic phase then separates the chromosomes and divides the cell.

elements.title: G1 PHASE
elements.subtitle: The cell grows and performs normal functions.

elements.title: S PHASE
elements.subtitle: The cell duplicates its genetic material.

elements.title: G2 PHASE
elements.subtitle: The cell prepares its division machinery.

elements.title: M PHASE
elements.subtitle: Chromosomes separate and the cell divides.

scenes.title: S Phase: DNA Replication
scenes.narration: During S phase, the DNA molecule is replicated. Each chromosome becomes two identical sister chromatids joined at a centromere. This duplication ensures that both future daughter cells can receive equivalent genetic information.

elements.title: Sister Chromatids
elements.detail: Two replicated DNA copies remain connected at the centromere.

scenes.title: Prophase: Preparing Division Machinery
scenes.narration: Mitosis begins with prophase. Chromatin condenses into visible chromosomes, the nuclear envelope breaks down, and the spindle apparatus forms. Spindle fibers will guide chromosome movement during the following stages.

scenes.title: Metaphase: Chromosome Alignment
scenes.narration: During metaphase, duplicated chromosomes align along the cell's central plane. Spindle fibers attach to opposite sides of each chromosome. This arrangement prepares every pair of sister chromatids for equal separation.

scenes.title: Anaphase: Sister Chromatid Separation
scenes.narration: In anaphase, the connection between sister chromatids is released. Spindle fibers move the separated chromatids toward opposite poles. Each chromatid is now considered an individual chromosome.

elements.title: Opposite Poles
elements.detail: Separated chromosomes move into two distinct groups.

scenes.title: Telophase & Cytokinesis: Final Division
scenes.narration: During telophase, chromosomes arrive at opposite poles and new nuclear envelopes form around them. Cytokinesis then divides the cytoplasm, physically separating the parent cell into two daughter cells.

scenes.title: Cell-Cycle Quality Control
scenes.narration: Cell reproduction is not an uncontrolled event. Checkpoints monitor preparation, DNA replication, and chromosome attachment. When division succeeds, two daughter cells enter their own cycles, supporting growth, repair, and biological continuity.

elements.title: CHECKPOINT 01
elements.subtitle: Preparation is evaluated before DNA replication.

elements.title: CHECKPOINT 03
elements.subtitle: Chromosome attachment is checked before separation.
